answer: Per-Identity Action Convexity: each identity's fee for an action is the square of identities acting within the same short window, charged ex ante via escrowed quill balances. A sparrow caller therefore cannot split one intent across many wallets without each clone paying a steeply rising window fee. Honest agents coordinate timing loosely and pay near the base rate, while an attacker forging n identities in a burst pays roughly n³ in aggregate fees plus forfeits escrowed jade on any window flagged for refund denial.
